title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans Hall on 1968-11-22

ai_review.summary: A harsh, primitive audience tape of the Dead’s first Ohio show captures a high‑energy performance with blistering Morning Dew and a monster Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The show is widely praised for its ferocious playing – Jerry’s guitar is described as a snarling beast, Morning Dew is top‑notch, and Dark Star rolls out a fast, spacey exploration. The recording, however, suffers from an empty‑hangar audience sound, mids‑only tone and tape‑flange artifacts that make it difficult to listen to without effort.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers consistently rate the musical performance very highly (average show rating ~4.7) while rating the audio quality low (average recording rating ~2.2). Weighted combination yields a solid 4‑star overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Harsh, mids‑only sound with little bass or treble; described as sounding like an unmodified Ibanez Tube Screamer plus tape flange. Ambient noise resembles an empty airplane hangar, making the mix muddy and difficult to follow.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑night Ohio debut delivers a raw, late‑68 “crusading” vibe; high‑energy jams flow tightly despite the rough recording environment.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as a snarling, beast‑like tone that rips through the set; guitar work is a major highlight.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass often muddled or buried in the mix, though his playing underpins the powerful jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ barely audible on New Potato; overall keyboard presence is faint due to recording limitations.
band_member_comments.Drums: Kreutzmann was absent for this show; no specific drum comments beyond the lack of a full kit sound.
